basis: Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with ventricular structural abnormalities and arrhythmias; no supported extracardiac involvement.
Immune deficiency, enteropathy and endocrinopathy define disease; bronchiectasis 30-79%. Bladder dysfunction 80-99%, skin, bone, blood and vascular manifestations omitted by cap.
Umbrella disorder of bilirubin metabolism; hepatic injury is not intrinsic to most forms, and neurologic injury is confined to severe subtypes.
Vertebrobasilar arterial insufficiency causes defining posterior cerebral ischemia; visual disturbance and vertigo reflect central dysfunction.
Reported defining constellation includes cutis aplasia/epidermolysis, cleft palate and ectrodactyly; ptosis/ectropion are defining eyelid anomalies, frequency unreported.
Congenital unilateral digital and metacarpal reduction; short nail remnants accompany the absent terminal digits rather than independent skin disease.
Interferonopathy with developmental impairment and leukodystrophy; inflammatory chilblains affect 8/14 patients (~57%).
Cranial hyperostosis/metaphyseal dysplasia; hearing loss 4/5, facial palsy 4/5 and optic atrophy 2/3 from compression. Common dental abnormalities omitted by cap.
Brachial plexus compression defines neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome; rib anomalies are predisposing anatomy, and myalgia does not establish muscle injury.
Congenital hypoplasia of the eyelid tarsal plates with absent lower eyelashes; the tarsus here is an eyelid structure.
Umbrella of iron metabolism and transport disorders; hepatic, hematologic and neurologic damage vary by subtype and are not universal group features.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss develop in most patients over the typical course.
Inherited deficiency of the circulating hemoglobin-binding protein haptoglobin; transfusion anaphylaxis is a risk, not intrinsic immune disease or organ injury.
HTRA1-associated age-related macular degeneration directly affects the retina and macula.
Inherited abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism with elevated reverse T3 and rT3/T3 ratio; no supported additional organ damage.
Sacral cutaneous hemangiomas establish skin involvement; unspecified congenital abnormalities and the Cowden parent do not establish additional organ involvement.
Infection-associated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS; endothelial injury with microvascular thrombosis is defining. Neurologic injury occurs in 5-29%.
Congenital bilateral absence of toes is a skeletal limb reduction defect.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by vertebral, epiphyseal and metaphyseal abnormalities, joint laxity and progressive spinal malalignment; other involvement varies by subtype.
Defining spectrum includes lumbosacral agenesis, anorectal malformations and urinary tract abnormalities. Individual specified neural defects occur in 1/4 patients.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss affects 19/19 reported patients.
Intellectual disability and eyelid malformations define disease; auditory canal stenosis 4/5, hearing loss 3/5 and joint hypermobility 5/5. Dental anomalies 2/4 omitted by cap.
Atrophoderma, milia, hypotrichosis and cutaneous tumors define this skin disorder; peripheral vasodilation/cyanosis does not establish damaging vascular disease.
Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle wasting and foot deformity follow denervation rather than a separate direct muscle or bone disease process.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a marrow and blood-cell malignancy; somatic WT1 mutation does not imply renal disease or inherited WT1 syndrome.
